question: The Commission’s proposed definition of recycled plastic, as outlined in the proposed end-of-life vehicles regulation1 (ELVR), diverges from previous definitions by the Joint Research Centre (JRC), introducing significant challenges to the regulation’s efficacy. The ELVR seeks to steer the automotive industry toward a circular model by establishing targets for recycled plastics.

However, discrepancies between the Commission’s definition of ‘plastic’ and the findings of the 2023 JRC Study on recycled plastic2 have raised concerns. The Commission’s definition of ‘plastic,’ as stated in Article 3.1(9) of the ELVR, is rooted in Article 3.5 of REACH3.

This definition encompasses materials such as elastomers, thermosets and process materials such as paints, adhesives and sealants, which are deemed non-recyclable or difficult to recycle according to the JRC study. In view of this: 1.
Why does the Commission’s plastic definition deviate from that used in the JRC study?
Does the Commission believe the recycling targets are achievable, especially considering the inclusion of materials such as elastomers and thermosets?
Will the Commission consider modifying its proposal to align the definition of plastic with that in the JRC study?

Proposal for a Regulation on circularity requirements for vehicle design and on management of end-of-life vehicles (COM(2023)0451). https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC129008. Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of 18 December 2006 concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/1907/2023-08-06.
